latin: Quodcunque contingens deus sciuit esse futurum, necessario sciuit illud esse futurum.

mentions.context: originate in the same place in Thomas’s Summa. Thesis 4 emphasizes that the contingent nature for us of each of the future contingencies, is from God’s per- spective, necessary, as a concomitant of the infallibility of divine knowledge;14 we have already seen these notions in Thomas (nn. 11–13). Thesis 5 states that, whatever future contingency God knows is known to Him in a neces- sary fashion.15 Necessity is emphasized again by Thomas a little later in the same discussion.16
